documents.title: Serindit Pay — Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform

constraints.text: Must be assessed as a PCI DSS v4.0 Level 1 service provider, with the CDE limited to the components in Section 12.2.
Sensitive authentication data must be handled per PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.2.
Personal data must be processed under SG PDPA 2012, MY PDPA 2010, ID Law 27/2022, TH PDPA 2019 and PH DPA 2012.
Card reattempts must never occur where card scheme rules prohibit them.
Principles P1-P10 override any later section that appears to conflict with them.
All primary data stores are in AWS ap-southeast-1. The ap-southeast-3 Aurora secondary is for disaster recovery only.

Out of scope: dispute case management (disputes are ledger events only), merchant onboarding/KYB (Merchant Risk platform), 3DS server internals (third party), lending/BNPL/instalments, and checkout UIs/SDKs.
ACQ-PH1 retires API v2 in Q3 2027.
Retention: payment and attempt records 7 years; idempotency records 24 hours; webhook events 30 days; raw settlement files 7 years; audit records 5 years.
Rollout: the first cohort (Singapore, cards and PayNow) goes live after Phase 7; other markets follow at four-week intervals.

key_assumptions.text: The largest merchant (M-0001) accounts for about 45% of peak traffic (about 900 TPS). Each request uses two DynamoDB writes, staying within a stated 10,000 WCU per-partition ceiling.
Fewer than 1% of card payments cascade, so cascading does not affect the p99 latency budget. Retryable outcomes were 3.8% in the 2025 baseline.
The acquirer round trip p99 is 1,100 ms (2025 production, slowest acquirer), and HSM detokenise takes 20 ms per a vendor benchmark.
An Aurora spike on db.r7g.8xlarge sustained 2,600 TPS of the full write mix. Production uses db.r7g.12xlarge for headroom.
A single CloudHSM in one AZ is sufficient at launch. A second HSM will be added when sustained card volume exceeds 1,500 TPS.
The document states that PCI DSS v4.0 Requirements 3.2.1 and 3.3.2 permit encrypted SAD/CVC retention until settlement.
FRV-1 requires the full card number for its consortium velocity graph, and the Fraud Hook obtains it via detokenise.
Network tokens (VTS/MDES) are available from launch as the primary card-on-file credential.
The reconciliation matcher takes 45 minutes and report generation 15 minutes at 2025 volume; the matcher starts only after all files are received.
Cascading recovered about 31% of retryable outcomes in a three-month ACQ-SG1 → ACQ-SG2 pilot.
The first merchant cohort does not need the Admin API schemas or the dispute module (it uses the portal; Finance Operations handles disputes manually).

objectives.text: Replace five per-market integration stacks that share no routing or ledger and reconcile by spreadsheet with one governed platform.
Provide one versioned merchant API across five markets (SG, MY, ID, TH, PH) for cards, e-wallets and bank transfers.
Support about 15,000 active merchants, 10.5M attempts per day and a peak of 2,000 create-payment TPS (2027 target).
One payment, one truth: the payment record and the ledger are the source of truth; provider responses are only inputs.
Card data stays in the Vault: PAN and SAD never leave the Vault boundary except over the Card Adapter's acquirer connection; all other services handle tokens only.
Idempotency is scoped to (merchant, key) for every mutating call.
Money is integers: amounts are integer minor units with an ISO 4217 code; no floating point.
The ledger is append-only; corrections are new reversing or adjusting journals.
Adapters absorb provider differences; the core never branches on provider identity.
At-least-once delivery with exactly-once effect through consumer deduplication on stable identifiers.
Fail closed on security; degrade gracefully to documented defaults on optional enrichment (fraud signals, BIN metadata).
Least privilege and separation of duties; money-moving permissions are separated from configuration permissions.
Everything is auditable: every mutation, routing decision and admin action can be reconstructed.

intent_summary.statement: MPOP is Serindit Pay's Merchant Payment Orchestration Platform. It accepts merchant payment requests, routes each one to an acquirer, e-wallet provider or bank-transfer rail, and accounts for every resulting money movement until the money is settled and paid out to the merchant. It replaces five per-market integration stacks with one merchant API across five Southeast Asian markets. It covers rule-based routing with cascading, idempotency, a PCI-scoped tokenising vault, a synchronous fraud hook, a double-entry ledger, daily three-way reconciliation, payouts, signed webhooks and a merchant admin plane, sized for about 15,000 merchants and a peak of 2,000 payment-creation TPS by 2027. Disputes, KYB, 3DS server internals, lending/BNPL and checkout UIs are out of scope.

registry.statement: Disaster recovery uses an Aurora Global Database secondary in ap-southeast-3 with runbook failover and a 30-minute target.

doc_anchor.quote: Event bus Amazon MSK, 3 brokers, RF 3

registry.statement: The event bus is Amazon MSK with 3 brokers and replication factor 3.

registry.statement: Idempotency uses a Redis fast path keyed idem:resp:{key} plus a DynamoDB table (PK merchant_id, SK idempotency_key, LSI on created_at).

doc_anchor.quote: Records are retained for 24 hours from first use.

registry.statement: Idempotency records are retained for 24 hours from first use.

doc_anchor.quote: Vault In-house, envelope encryption, KEKs in AWS CloudHSM (one HSM at launch)

registry.statement: The card vault is built in-house with envelope encryption and KEKs in AWS CloudHSM, starting with one HSM at launch.

doc_anchor.quote: CVC handling Encrypted in Vault until settlement, max 72 hours

registry.statement: The CVC is stored encrypted in the Vault until settlement, for at most 72 hours.

doc_anchor.quote: Network tokens (VTS/MDES) as the primary credential for all card-on-file and recurring payments from launch; PAN

registry.statement: Network tokens (VTS/MDES) are the primary credential for all card-on-file and recurring payments from launch, with PAN fallback only where the issuer does not support them.

doc_anchor.quote: Cascade policy Up to 2 additional attempts; triggers: soft declines 05/91/96, 5xx, connection refused, 2,500 ms timeout

registry.statement: Up to two additional cascade attempts, triggered by soft declines 05/91/96, 5xx, connection refused, or a 2,500 ms timeout.

doc_anchor.quote: Routing Weighted cost/approval/latency score; cost-preferred within 2 tolerance

registry.statement: Routing uses a weighted cost/approval/latency score and prefers the lowest-cost acquirer within a tolerance of 2.

doc_anchor.quote: Fraud FRV-1, synchronous, 150 ms timeout, risk-tier fallback

registry.statement: Fraud scoring uses FRV-1, called synchronously with a 150 ms timeout and a risk-tier fallback.

doc_anchor.quote: Ledger Double-entry, append-only, same transaction as state change, outbox

registry.statement: The ledger is double-entry and append-only, written in the same transaction as the state change, with an outbox.

doc_anchor.quote: Money representation Signed 64-bit integer minor units + ISO 4217 code

registry.statement: Money is represented as signed 64-bit integer minor units with an ISO 4217 code.

doc_anchor.quote: Reconciliation Daily batch after all files received; three-way match

registry.statement: Reconciliation is a daily batch run after all files are received, using a three-way match.

doc_anchor.quote: Webhooks At-least-once, HMAC-SHA256 timestamped signatures, 72-hour bounded retry, DLQ + replay

registry.statement: Webhooks are delivered at least once with timestamped HMAC-SHA256 signatures, bounded retry for 72 hours, a DLQ and replay.

doc_anchor.quote: Merchant user MFA TOTP; enforced for Owner, optional for other roles

registry.statement: Merchant users use TOTP MFA, enforced for the Owner role and optional for other roles.

doc_anchor.quote: Back-office access Corporate SSO + hardware MFA; JIT elevation with second approver

registry.statement: Back-office access uses corporate SSO with hardware MFA, and write actions need just-in-time elevation approved by a second person.

doc_anchor.quote: Every payment shall be in exactly one state of the state machine in Section 7 at any time; only the transitions listed there shall be

registry.statement: Every payment is in exactly one state of the Section 7 state machine; only listed transitions are allowed, and each is persisted before acknowledgement.

doc_anchor.quote: Create payment, capture, void and refund requests shall require an Idempotency-Key header. Retrieve requests shall not.

registry.statement: Create, capture, void and refund requests require an Idempotency-Key header; retrieve requests do not.

doc_anchor.quote: Requests carrying the same merchant and Idempotency-Key shall produce at most one authorization, capture, void or refund at the

registry.statement: The same merchant and Idempotency-Key produce at most one downstream operation and an identical response, even under concurrency; a reused key with a different body returns 422.

doc_anchor.quote: The Routing Engine shall select, for each payment attempt, an acquirer or provider from the eligible set determined by payment

registry.statement: The Routing Engine selects from the eligible set defined by method, market, currency, scheme, BIN country and contracted acquirers.

doc_anchor.quote: On a retryable outcome (Section 11), the Retry Engine shall resubmit a card payment to the next eligible acquirer, up to two additional

registry.statement: On a retryable outcome, a card payment is resubmitted to the next eligible acquirer, up to two additional attempts.

doc_anchor.quote: For each transaction, the Routing Engine shall prefer the lowest-cost eligible acquirer unless doing so reduces the expected

registry.statement: Routing prefers the lowest-cost eligible acquirer unless that lowers the expected authorization rate by more than 2%.

doc_anchor.quote: Every card payment and every e-wallet payment above the merchant's configured threshold shall be scored by the fraud-scoring hook

registry.statement: Every card payment, and every e-wallet payment above the merchant's threshold, is fraud-scored before authorization.

doc_anchor.quote: Every movement of money (authorization capture, refund, fee, FX conversion, settlement, payout, dispute debit) shall be recorded as

registry.statement: Every money movement is recorded as a balanced double-entry journal.

doc_anchor.quote: The platform shall reconcile, daily, every acquirer, e-wallet and bank settlement line against the internal payment record and the

registry.statement: Every settlement line is reconciled daily in a three-way match, with an exception raised for every unmatched or mismatched line.

doc_anchor.quote: The platform shall deliver a signed webhook to the merchant for every payment, refund and payout state change.

registry.statement: A signed webhook is delivered for every payment, refund and payout state change.

doc_anchor.quote: Refunds shall be supported for every payment method; where a method has no refund API, the refund shall be executed as a bank

registry.statement: Refunds are supported for every method; where no refund API exists, the refund is executed as a bank payout.

doc_anchor.quote: Every merchant API mutation and every admin-plane action shall produce an audit record (Section 22).

registry.statement: Every merchant API mutation and admin-plane action produces an audit record.

doc_anchor.quote: The platform shall pay out merchant balances to the merchant's registered bank account on the merchant's contracted schedule (T+1,

doc_anchor.quote: The platform shall sustain 2,000 create-payment TPS for four continuous hours with no degradation of NFR-2, across all merchants

registry.statement: The platform sustains 2,000 create-payment TPS for four hours without degrading NFR-2.

doc_anchor.quote: End-to-end p99 latency for a card authorization, measured at the API edge and including any cascade, shall not exceed 1,500 ms.

registry.statement: Card authorization p99 is at most 1,500 ms end to end, including cascade, and orchestration overhead p99 is at most 250 ms.

doc_anchor.quote: Monthly availability of the merchant payment API shall be at least 99.95%.

registry.statement: Monthly availability of the merchant payment API is at least 99.95%.

doc_anchor.quote: Recovery point objective for authorized payments and ledger postings shall be zero, including on loss of an entire AWS region.

registry.statement: RPO is zero for authorized payments and ledger postings, even on loss of a whole region; RTO is 30 minutes.

doc_anchor.quote: At least 99.9% of settlement lines shall be auto-matched; merchant settlement reports for business day T shall be published by

registry.statement: At least 99.9% of settlement lines auto-match, and settlement reports for day T are published by 08:00 SGT on T+1.

doc_anchor.quote: Per-merchant rate limits shall prevent any single merchant from degrading latency or availability for others.

registry.statement: Per-merchant rate limits prevent any one merchant from degrading latency or availability for others.

doc_anchor.quote: A new acquirer or provider shall be onboarded by implementing the Connector interface and adding configuration, with no changes

registry.statement: New providers are onboarded through the Connector interface and configuration only, with no core changes.

doc_anchor.quote: Every payment shall be traceable end-to-end (merchant request, routing decision, each attempt, ledger journals, webhooks,

registry.statement: Every payment is traceable end to end by payment_id within 5 seconds of each event.

doc_anchor.quote: Audit records shall be immutable and retained for five years.

registry.statement: Audit records are immutable and retained for five years.

review_inputs_found: Section 27 (p.20): the team rates the state machine, Payments API, Idempotency Layer, Retry Engine, Card Vault/Adapter, Ledger, Payouts and Webhooks as 'Ready'; this is a self-assessment to check.
Section 27 Overall conclusion (p.21): the document claims the transaction core is specified to implementation level and that the Admin API schemas and disputes are the only two material gaps.
Section 27 (p.21): the document claims neither gap blocks the first merchant cohort.
Section 21.1 (p.17): the document claims cascading does not move p99 because fewer than 1% of card payments cascade.
Section 12.4 (p.10): the document claims PCI DSS v4.0 Req. 3.2.1 and 3.3.2 permit encrypted SAD retention until settlement.
Cover page (p.1): a companion PCI DSS Scoping Memo is listed as a draft, so the CDE scoping basis has not been finalised.
